answer: Each applicant cuts a lens from one onyx block from its own summit; its veins throw a spectrum no other block shares. Each round the registry shines light through a prism at a set angle; the holder logs the cast spectrum, and the next angle is hashed from that spectrum and the holder's key, so readings depend on the last, fitting no other lens. Splitting the block ruins both spectra, so one block serves one identity. Each further identity needs a new summit, block, and lens: $360, 17 summit-days; 5,000 fakes need 5,000 summits, $1.8m and 85,000 summit-days, and no surveyor certifies two peaks.
